theory.intro: Triangles can be named by comparing the lengths of their sides. Equal sides are shown with matching tick marks.
facts: **Equilateral**: all three sides equal (all three angles equal too).
**Scalene**: all three sides different — no equal sides.
steps: Look at the tick marks (or given lengths) on each side.
Count how many sides are equal.
Three equal $\Rightarrow$ equilateral; two equal $\Rightarrow$ isosceles; none equal $\Rightarrow$ scalene.

foundation.solution_text:
The single ticks show $AB=AC$.
Exactly two sides are equal.
$\Delta ABC$ is isosceles.

The single ticks show $DE=EF=FD$.
All three sides are equal.
$\Delta DEF$ is equilateral.

The three side lengths are $5\text{ cm}$, $7\text{ cm}$ and $9\text{ cm}$.
No two of them are equal.
The triangle is scalene.

The two slant sides are both $8\text{ cm}$, and the base is $11\text{ cm}$.
Exactly two sides are equal.
The triangle is isosceles.

The largest angle is $70^{\circ}$.
$70^{\circ}<90^{\circ}$, so every angle is less than $90^{\circ}$.
The triangle is acute-angled.

The largest angle is $105^{\circ}$.
$105^{\circ}>90^{\circ}$, so one angle is obtuse.
The triangle is obtuse-angled.

The small square at $Q$ marks an angle of $90^{\circ}$.
$\Delta PQR$ is right-angled.

Reading clockwise from $X$, the vertices are $X$, then $Y$, then $Z$.
The triangle is $\Delta XYZ$.

foundation.question_text: A triangle has no two sides of equal length. Name this type of triangle.
foundation.solution_text:
None of the three sides are equal.
The triangle is scalene.

foundation.question_text: A triangle has an angle of $91^{\circ}$. Classify the triangle according to its angle properties.
foundation.solution_text:
$91^{\circ}>90^{\circ}$, so one angle is obtuse.
The triangle is obtuse-angled.

mastery.question_text: In $\Delta DEF$, $DE=EF$ and $\angle DEF=90^{\circ}$. Classify $\Delta DEF$ by its sides and by its angles, and name the two equal angles using vertex letters.
A triangle has angles $45^{\circ}$, $45^{\circ}$ and $90^{\circ}$. Tom says it must be right-angled. Katie says it must be isosceles. Decide whether each student is correct, and explain why.
mastery.solution_text:
One angle is $90^{\circ}$, so the triangle is right-angled and Tom is correct.
Two angles are equal, so the two sides opposite them are equal and the triangle is isosceles, so Katie is correct.
Side names and angle names describe two separate properties, so both students are correct.

mastery.question_text:
The table below sorts triangles by their side property and their angle property.
$\begin{array}{l|c|c|c} & \text{Isosceles} & \text{Equilateral} & \text{Scalene} \\ \hline \text{Acute} & & & \\ \hline \text{Right} & & & \\ \hline \text{Obtuse} & & & \end{array}$
Two cells of the table can never be filled. Name them and explain why.
mastery.solution_text:
Every angle of an equilateral triangle is $60^{\circ}$.
$60^{\circ}<90^{\circ}$, so an equilateral triangle can never contain a right angle or an obtuse angle.
The two cells that can never be filled are equilateral–right and equilateral–obtuse.

mastery.question_text: Anika claims that every isosceles triangle is acute-angled. Give a labelled triangle that shows her claim is false, and state its full classification.
